summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — GPN +10%, TPR +5%, ECHO +4%, GIS +4%, MKC +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 3 downside moves (SNDK -15%, BE -15%, LITE -14%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SNDK (-15.45%) — No confirmed Nov 23 catalyst found. Likely a continuation of the mid-November AI-hardware/memory sell-off (SNDK fell 5-8% on Nov 10 and Nov 13 amid AI-hardware weakness); unverified for today. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: SNDK is a recently spun-off, highly volatile mid-cap NAND/memory name. After a run of double-digit drops, a momentum or mean-reversion filter would also likely reject it on gap size and volatility.

top_movers.catalyst: Bloomberg report that GTCR, Global Payments' largest shareholder, is exploring a ~$50B take-private with other PE firms; no decision yet. Sources conflict on timing (Nov 20 vs Nov 23).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: GPN is a large-cap payments name that no strategy includes. The jump was an unscheduled M&A headline, which a technical momentum or mean-reversion bot would only see after the gap had already happened.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive rule that admits any S&P 500 name into a watchlist when its gap is ≥+8% on takeover or 'exploring sale' headlines, and cap the position size because the deal is unconfirmed and could fail.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-23 — likely sector/consumer-discretionary rally (holiday-season luxury/handbag sentiment) or technical bounce after the post-August FY27 outlook selloff.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: TPR is a mid-cap luxury/accessories name that no strategy lists. A +5.4% move with no identifiable catalyst also wouldn't trip a news-reactive trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unlisted mover' scan that admits any US stock with market cap >$5B, 20-day avg volume >2M and close-to-close move ≥+4% to the momentum-trader candidate pool for the next session.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-23; searches turned up no same-day story. Ticker ambiguity: ECHO is Echo Global Logistics, which was taken private in 2021, and EchoStar trades as SATS.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ECHO looks like a small/mid-cap, thinly covered name (close 87.865), and a +4.28% move without news is likely a sector or technical drift that no news-reactive filter would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unclaimed movers' scan that admits names with ≥+4% close-to-close on ≥1.5× 20-day average volume, with a dollar-volume floor, to a watch-only universe so repeats can be backtested before going live.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found; likely a rebound in beaten-down packaged-food/staples names. Backdrop: Häagen-Dazs ex-North America separation report (WSJ) and the CEO succession announcement.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: GIS is a large-cap defensive consumer-staples stock near its 52-week low. A +3.65% drift with no earnings or gap catalyst likely wouldn't pass momentum or news-reactive filters anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — a low-volatility staples bounce with no catalyst is not worth widening the universe for; if desired, add a staples-sector mean-reversion sleeve keyed to distance from the 52-week low.)

top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta AI-power/clean-energy names such as BE to the mean-reversion universe, with an entry gate of a ≥12% one-day drop, no earnings that day, and volume ≥2× the 20-day average. Alternatively, treat this as a no-op if shorting isn't supported.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst — searches found no NVDA reports dated 2026-11-23. A -14% one-day move on a mega-cap with no news suggests a sector/AI-trade selloff, or a bad price or split-adjustment in the data feed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. NVDA is a mega-cap semiconductor, and the strategies that trade it (news-reactive-sentiment-gate, insider-cluster-momentum) need a news or insider-buy signal. Neither fired with no catalyst. Long-only strategies also can't profit from a drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a data-sanity check that flags any |close-to-close| ≥10% move in a ≥$1T-cap name with no matching news hit, to separate feed or split errors from real moves. Then add a cross-sectional 'AI-semis drawdown' regime flag to the sentiment gate.

top_movers.catalyst: No LITE-specific news found for 11/23. Likely a continuation of the AI-optics/photonics selloff (hyperscaler-capex fears), with LITE also tied to Marvell's slide through the pending fixed-ratio all-stock deal.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LITE is a mid/large-cap optical-components name that no strategy includes. It was also in a multi-week sector downtrend, so a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot would have no clean entry.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for this one, since it needs short capability or a sector-wide risk-off signal. If wanted, add a sector-drawdown flag (e.g. optics basket down ≥10% in 5 days) that blocks new longs in AI-hardware names.
